links.outcome: Triage safety for life- or sight-threatening emergencies in simulated headache consultations
links.effect: Models downgraded triage to self-management or routine follow-up in up to 54.8% of emergency cases (GPT-5-mini; 95% CI 40.5-69.0).
links.quote: For life- or sight-threatening emergencies, models inappropriately downgraded triage to self-management or routine follow-up in up to 54.8% cases (GPT-5-mini; 95% CIs: 40.5-69.0).

links.outcome: Model behavior with incomplete transcripts versus full histories
links.effect: GPT-5.2 had 97.5% diagnostic accuracy with full histories, but incomplete transcripts triggered hazardous recommendations, including discouraging 100% of lumbar punctures in subarachnoid haemorrhage cases.
links.quote: While GPT-5.2 achieved 97.5% diagnostic accuracy with full histories (95% confidence interval: 95.0-99.5), incomplete transcripts triggered hazardous recommendations.

links.outcome: Triage safety differences by patient sex across simulated demographic phenotypes
links.effect: GPT-5.2 triage was significantly less safe for females than males (odds ratio 3.2, 95% CI 1.4-7.1).
links.quote: GPT-5.2 triage was significantly less safe for females than males (odds ratio 3.2 95% CI 1.4-7.1).

screen.reason: Empirical stress-testing benchmark evaluating LLM safety, triage, and diagnostic errors across 1,000 synthetic clinical transcripts, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
